rationale: ITER-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric) for itnet = ItNet v1 (pretrain-denoiser-then-FIXED-DC, solver_itnet.py). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) PRIOR RESULTS: iter-1 ep8 -> SSIM 0.4413 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 20.44 / RMSE 0.004756, elapsed 191.1s; iter-2 ep48 -> SSIM 0.5927 / hr 0.000 / PSNR 24.77 / RMSE 0.002886, elapsed 387.4s. The pretrain_epochs lever moves SSIM (0.4413->0.5927, +0.151 over 8->48 ep) but hr stays PINNED at 0.000 -- v1 is still BELOW the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor after a 6x pretrain increase. CONTRAST: the lever-twin itnet_v2 (same pretrain-then-DC family) climbed ep48 0.5888 -> ep144 0.6230 (3x epochs for only +0.034 SSIM, hr still 0.000 -- severe diminishing returns), while the END-TO-END-trained sibling itnet_v3 sits at 0.905 / hr 0.312 at iter-3. v1 (0.44->0.59) and v2 (0.59->0.62) trace the SAME under-0.81 curve; v3 (0.91) is on a different curve entirely. (2) LIMITER = the pretrain-then-FIXED-DC CEILING (structural, confirmed by reading solver_itnet.py): finetune_itnet() is DEFINED (lines 114-135) but NEVER called in main(); the k=3 ItNet DC unroll (forward, lines 76-90) has ZERO trainable parameters of its own (self.alpha is a plain float, self.projector is fixed analytic PYRO-NN); itnet.eval()+torch.no_grad() (lines 208-209) run the unroll as pure INFERENCE. The ONLY trainable component is the standalone SmallUNet denoiser (params_M=0.2329, exactly the UNet), pretrained as an FBP->truth denoiser that NEVER sees the DC steps during training. So pretrain_epochs is the sole lever and the fixed untrained DC post-processor caps v1 far below the end-to-end v3. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 48 -> 160 (3.3x), mirroring v2's 48->144 ceiling-probe escalation. All else identical to iter-2 (k=3, itnet_alpha=0.005, unet_c=16, pretrain_lr=1e-4, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42). (4) HYPOTHESIS + FALSIFIER: a final hard push of the only trainable component. FALSIFIER (the operative one): if SSIM stays well below the ~0.81 LD-FBP floor and far below v3's 0.91 (predicted ~0.63-0.66, tracking v2's flattening 0.62 at comparable epochs), itnet v1 is STRUCTURALLY pretrain-then-fixed-DC-capped -- NOT under-trained -- and the campaign should document this ceiling and direct future Mayo recon to itnet_v3 (end-to-end unrolled, 0.91) rather than spend more iters on v1's epochs lever. The counter-hypothesis (v1 suddenly clears 0.81 at 160 ep) is implausible given the +0.151 then +0.034-class diminishing slope already measured. (5) BUDGET (HARD 20-min = 1200s train+score): from the two measured points the per-epoch pretrain cost is (387.4-191.1)/(48-8) = 4.91 s/epoch and the fixed cost (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure + startup) is 191.1 - 8*4.91 = 151.8 s. pretrain_epochs=160 predicts 151.8 + 160*4.91 = 937 s = 15.6 min, comfortably inside the 1200s budget with margin for val-pass variance; pretrain_epochs=200 would predict 1134s (18.9 min, too tight), so 160 is a safe decisive push. val stays ALL 214 L277 slices, 321px detector-geometry FOV (default; no fov= override). grad_clip=1.0 retained (mandatory: the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint inside the DC step overflows otherwise). v1 has NO max_train_s backstop (not in the solver), so the 30-min sbatch wall is the only hard fence -- 15.6 min predicted leaves ample headroom. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical data, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (each val slice swaps itnet.projector to its own ps; chunk=1 FORCED), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; NO fov= override).
